subject.title: [Feature]: Fallback approval mode + model attribution in messages

question: Should OpenClaw add a core opt-in approval gate before executing configured model fallbacks, and what should the config, timeout, denial, and no-approval-route behavior be?
rationale: The remaining request changes fallback runtime semantics and adds config surface; repository policy treats fallback behavior and config/default additions as product- and compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Design a core opt-in fallback gate
options.body: Define a default-off per-agent or per-session approval contract that uses existing approval delivery where possible and specifies timeout and deny behavior before coding.

options.title: Keep automatic fallback with visibility only
options.body: Treat responsePrefix model attribution and fallback notices as the supported transparency model, leaving fallback execution automatic.

options.title: Route through plugin/API design first
options.body: Add or extend an approval/fallback hook surface so plugins can own policy before adding a core config key.

recommendation.title: Design a core opt-in fallback gate
recommendation.body: Define a default-off per-agent or per-session approval contract that uses existing approval delivery where possible and specifies timeout and deny behavior before coding.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current-history route for the fallback runtime, config-sensitive surface, and model-failover docs.
